newsitem.title: USA: Suffolk Cty, N.Y., cost in TWA crash tops $4 mln.
newsitem.headline: Suffolk Cty, N.Y., cost in TWA crash tops $4 mln.

text.p: The municipal cost to Suffolk County, N.Y., for the clean up and investigation into the cause of TWA Flight 800 has reached $4.4 million dollars and is still growing, the county's budget director said Tuesday.
Kenneth Weiss said the county has paid $1.3 million in salaries and $1.6 million in overtime wages to police and other county workers since the watery crash of the coast of Long Island on July 17.
Also on the tab was DNA testing equipment that cost about $181,000 and a reconstructed helicopter landing pad totaling $60,000.

Although the county's 1996 budget comes in around $1.6 billion, the extraordinary expenses have sent Weiss and his staff scrambling to find flexibility in other budget areas that can absorb the added cost.
"We're looking at that right now. There's a lot (of expense) we're aware of, but haven't been charged yet. Police overtime may be a problem," Weiss said.
"Ultimately, we expect to be reimbursed by the federal government or some other agency. Right now it's a question of funding (the hardest-hit departments) through the rest of 1996.
"We're in the process now of doing the 1997 budget and we're looking for areas we may be over in to temporarily cover the cost of the disaster," Weiss said.
